Vienna.name: Kunsthistorisches Museum
Vienna.description: The Habsburgs’ art collection in a palace-sized museum on the Ringstrasse: Bruegel, Vermeer, Rembrandt, and a café under the dome.

Vienna.name: St Stephen’s Cathedral
Vienna.description: Vienna’s Gothic cathedral and the square around it, at the dead centre of the old town. Look up for the patterned tile roof.

Vienna.name: Hofburg palace
Vienna.description: The Habsburgs’ sprawling city palace: the imperial treasury, the Sisi Museum, the Spanish Riding School, the old library and the big square in front.

Vienna.name: Vienna State Opera
Vienna.description: One of the world’s great opera houses, on the Ringstrasse. Standing places go on sale shortly before most performances.

Vienna.name: Upper Belvedere
Vienna.description: A baroque palace turned art museum, home to Klimt’s The Kiss and a big collection of Austrian painting.

Vienna.name: Leopold Museum
Vienna.description: A white-cube museum in the MuseumsQuartier with the world’s largest collection of Egon Schiele, plus Klimt and Vienna 1900 design.

Vienna.name: Albertina
Vienna.description: A former Habsburg palace holding one of the great collections of drawings and prints, from Dürer’s hare to Picasso.

Vienna.name: Café Central
Vienna.description: The grandest of the old coffee houses, under vaulted ceilings in a former bank. Trotsky and Freud were regulars.

Vienna.name: Sigmund Freud Museum
Vienna.description: The apartment and consulting rooms where Freud lived and worked for 47 years, until he fled the Nazis in 1938.

Vienna.name: Mozarthaus
Vienna.description: The only one of Mozart’s Vienna homes that survives, where he wrote The Marriage of Figaro.

Vienna.name: Central Cemetery
Vienna.description: A huge park-like cemetery on the edge of town, with the graves of Beethoven, Schubert, Brahms and the Strauss family.

Vienna.name: Beethoven Museum
Vienna.description: The village house in Heiligenstadt where Beethoven, going deaf, wrote his despairing letter to his brothers.

Vienna.name: Imperial Crypt
Vienna.description: The burial vault of the Habsburgs, under a plain Capuchin church: 150 coffins, some of them elaborately decorated.

Vienna.name: Schönbrunn Palace
Vienna.description: The Habsburgs’ summer palace and gardens, a short metro ride from the centre.

Vienna.name: Giant Ferris Wheel
Vienna.description: The 1897 Ferris wheel in the Prater amusement park, with wooden cabins and a famous scene in The Third Man.

Vienna.name: Musikverein
Vienna.description: The concert hall with the golden main hall, home of the Vienna Philharmonic and its New Year’s Concert.

Vienna.name: Secession
Vienna.description: The art nouveau exhibition hall with the golden dome of leaves, built by Klimt’s breakaway group of artists. Klimt’s Beethoven Frieze is in the basement.

Vienna.name: Karl-Marx-Hof
Vienna.description: A kilometre-long block of public housing built in 1927–30, the showpiece of ‘Red Vienna’ and its social housing programme.

Amsterdam.name: Rijksmuseum
Amsterdam.description: The Netherlands’ national museum, in a grand 1885 building: Rembrandt’s The Night Watch, Vermeer and Dutch Golden Age art.

Amsterdam.name: Amsterdam Centraal
Amsterdam.description: The city’s main railway station, a brick palace of a building on the waterfront that opened in 1889.

Amsterdam.name: Dam Square
Amsterdam.description: The city’s main square, with the Royal Palace, the Nieuwe Kerk and the white National Monument to the Second World War.

Amsterdam.name: Van Gogh Museum
Amsterdam.description: The world’s largest collection of Van Gogh’s paintings, drawings and letters, on Museumplein.

Amsterdam.name: Oude Kerk
Amsterdam.description: Amsterdam’s oldest building, a medieval church in the middle of the red-light district, now also used for contemporary art.

Amsterdam.name: Waag
Amsterdam.description: A 15th-century city gate later used as a weigh house, standing in the middle of Nieuwmarkt square. It is now a restaurant.

Amsterdam.name: Anne Frank House
Amsterdam.description: The canal house where Anne Frank and her family hid from the Nazis for two years. The secret annexe is now a museum.

Amsterdam.name: Flower Market
Amsterdam.description: A flower market on a row of floating stalls along the Singel canal, selling bulbs, plants and cut flowers.

Amsterdam.name: East India House
Amsterdam.description: The 17th-century headquarters of the Dutch East India Company (VOC), now part of the University of Amsterdam.

Amsterdam.name: Vondelpark
Amsterdam.description: The city’s best-known park, opened in 1865 just south of the centre, with ponds, lawns and cycle paths.

Amsterdam.name: Dutch Resistance Museum
Amsterdam.description: A museum about the Dutch Resistance and daily life in Amsterdam under German occupation in the Second World War.

Amsterdam.name: Leidseplein
Amsterdam.description: A busy square on the edge of the canal ring, lined with theatres, bars and music venues.

Amsterdam.name: De Hallen
Amsterdam.description: A former tram depot from the early 1900s, converted into a food hall, a cinema and denim workshops.

Athens.name: Acropolis
Athens.description: The rock above the city with the ruins of the Parthenon, the Erechtheion and, on the south slope, the Theatre of Dionysus.

Athens.name: Syntagma Square
places: Tomb of the Unknown Soldier, Syntagma Square
Athens.description: The square in front of the Greek parliament, scene of the city’s big protests. Guards change at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier.

Athens.name: National Archaeological Museum
Athens.description: Greece’s largest archaeological museum, with ancient sculpture, bronzes, gold from Mycenae and the Antikythera mechanism.

Athens.name: Acropolis Museum
Athens.description: A modern glass museum at the foot of the Acropolis, holding the sculptures and finds from the hill.

Athens.name: Ancient Agora
Athens.description: The ruins of ancient Athens’ marketplace and civic centre, with the Temple of Hephaestus and the rebuilt Stoa of Attalos.

Athens.name: Kerameikos
Athens.description: The ancient city cemetery just outside the old walls, with grave monuments along the Street of Tombs and a small museum.

Athens.name: Pnyx
Athens.description: The hill where the citizens’ assembly of ancient Athens met, with a view across to the Acropolis.

Athens.name: Omonia Square
Athens.description: One of the city’s main squares, a busy traffic hub where several big avenues meet.

Athens.name: Exarchia Square
Athens.description: The central square of Exarchia, a neighbourhood long known for students, bookshops and left-wing and anarchist politics.

Athens.name: Athens Polytechnic
Athens.description: The 19th-century university campus where a tank broke through the gate to end the student uprising against the junta in November 1973.

Barcelona.name: Sagrada Família
Barcelona.description: Gaudí’s vast basilica, under construction since 1882, with tree-like columns inside and stained glass that fills it with colour.

Barcelona.name: Plaça de Catalunya
Barcelona.description: The big square at the top of La Rambla, where the old city meets the 19th-century Eixample grid.

Barcelona.name: Plaça de Sant Jaume
Barcelona.description: The square at the heart of the Gothic Quarter, where the Catalan government palace and the city hall face each other.

Barcelona.name: Camp Nou
Barcelona.description: FC Barcelona’s home stadium since 1957 and the largest in Europe. It is being rebuilt in stages.

Barcelona.name: Palau de la Música Catalana
places: Palau de la Música Catalana concert hall
Barcelona.description: A modernista concert hall from 1908, covered in mosaics, with a stained-glass skylight over the auditorium.

Barcelona.name: National Art Museum of Catalonia
Barcelona.description: Catalonia’s national art museum, in a palace on Montjuïc built for the 1929 exhibition, known for its Romanesque church murals.

Barcelona.name: Telefónica building
Barcelona.description: The telephone exchange on Plaça de Catalunya that was fought over in the street battles of May 1937, during the Spanish Civil War.

Barcelona.name: Olympic Stadium
Barcelona.description: The stadium on Montjuïc built for the 1929 exhibition and rebuilt as the main stadium of the 1992 Olympics.

Barcelona.name: La Model prison
Barcelona.description: A prison built in 1904 in the Eixample, used to hold political prisoners under Franco. It closed in 2017 and is now open to visitors.

Barcelona.name: Park Güell
Barcelona.description: Gaudí’s hillside park, with mosaic benches, gingerbread-like gatehouses and views over the city.

Barcelona.name: Santa Maria del Mar
Barcelona.description: A 14th-century Gothic church in El Born. The memorial square beside it marks the graves of those killed in the 1714 siege.

Belgrade.name: National Assembly
Belgrade.description: Serbia’s domed parliament building, finished in 1936. Protesters stormed it on 5 October 2000, bringing down Milošević.

Belgrade.name: Belgrade Fortress (Kalemegdan)
Belgrade.description: The old fortress on the ridge where the Sava meets the Danube, now a large park with walls, gates and river views.

Belgrade.name: House of Flowers
Belgrade.description: Tito’s mausoleum, a winter garden where he and his wife are buried, part of the Museum of Yugoslavia.

Belgrade.name: Slavija Square
Belgrade.description: A large roundabout square at the south end of the centre, where several main streets meet.

Belgrade.name: Western City Gate (Genex Tower)
Belgrade.description: A Brutalist pair of towers from 1977–80 at the entrance to New Belgrade, linked by a bridge with a round restaurant on top.

Belgrade.name: Former Chinese embassy site
places: Chinese Cultural Centre (site of 1999 embassy bombing)
Belgrade.description: The site of the Chinese embassy that NATO bombed in May 1999, killing three people. A Chinese cultural centre now stands there.

Belgrade.name: Nikola Tesla Museum
Belgrade.description: A museum of Tesla’s papers, inventions and working models, in a villa in the centre. His ashes are kept there in a gilded sphere.

Belgrade.name: Red Star Stadium
Belgrade.description: Red Star Belgrade’s football stadium, nicknamed the Marakana, and the biggest stadium in Serbia.

Berlin.name: Gemäldegalerie
Berlin.description: Berlin’s main museum of European painting from the 13th to 18th centuries, at the Kulturforum: Rembrandt, Vermeer, Caravaggio, Bruegel.

Berlin.name: Alte Nationalgalerie
Berlin.description: A temple-like museum on Museum Island with 19th-century painting and sculpture, including Caspar David Friedrich.

Berlin.name: Neues Museum
Berlin.description: A museum on Museum Island, rebuilt after war damage, with Egyptian and prehistoric collections. The bust of Nefertiti is here.

Berlin.name: Pergamon Museum
Berlin.description: The museum on Museum Island with the Ishtar Gate of Babylon and the Pergamon Altar. It is closed for a long renovation.

Berlin.name: Lustgarten
Berlin.description: The lawn in front of the Altes Museum and Berlin Cathedral on Museum Island, once a royal garden and parade ground.

Berlin.name: Brandenburg Gate
Berlin.description: The 18th-century city gate at the end of Unter den Linden, cut off just inside East Berlin while the Wall stood.

Berlin.name: Reichstag
Berlin.description: The German parliament building, with a glass dome you can climb for free if you book ahead.

Berlin.name: Alexanderplatz
Berlin.description: A big open square in former East Berlin, with the TV tower, the World Clock and a busy train station.

Berlin.name: Potsdamer Platz
Berlin.description: A busy square cut in two by the Wall and rebuilt in the 1990s with office towers and the Sony Center.

Berlin.name: Checkpoint Charlie
Berlin.description: The best-known crossing point between East and West Berlin during the Cold War, with a replica guard hut.

Berlin.name: Berghain
Berlin.description: A techno club in a former power station, open from Saturday night into Monday, with a strict door policy.

Berlin.name: Berlin Wall Memorial
Berlin.description: The main memorial to the Berlin Wall, along Bernauer Straße, with a preserved stretch of the border strip and a watchtower.

Berlin.name: Stasi Museum
Berlin.description: The former headquarters of East Germany’s secret police, with the minister’s offices kept as they were.

Berlin.name: Victory Column
Berlin.description: A tall 19th-century column topped by a gilded Victory, in the middle of the Tiergarten, with a viewing platform.

Berlin.name: Olympic Stadium
Berlin.description: The stadium built for the 1936 Olympics, now home to Hertha BSC and the German Cup final.

Berlin.name: SO36
Berlin.description: A punk and alternative music club in Kreuzberg, open since 1978.

Berlin.name: DDR Museum
Berlin.description: A hands-on museum about everyday life in East Germany, beside the Spree opposite Museum Island.

Brussels.name: Grand-Place
Brussels.description: The city’s central square, surrounded by ornate guild houses and the Gothic town hall.

Brussels.name: Belgian Comic Strip Center
Brussels.description: A museum of Belgian comics, from Tintin onwards, in an art nouveau former textile warehouse designed by Victor Horta.

Brussels.name: Atomium
Brussels.description: A 102-metre steel model of an iron crystal, built for the 1958 World’s Fair, with exhibitions and a view from the top sphere.

Brussels.name: Coudenberg Palace
Brussels.description: The underground remains of the old palace of the dukes of Brabant, which burned down in 1731, beneath Place Royale.

Brussels.name: Bourse
Brussels.description: The 19th-century former stock exchange in the centre, now home to a museum of Belgian beer.

Brussels.name: Tir National memorial
places: Tir National memorial (Edith Cavell execution site)
Brussels.description: A memorial ground on the site of the old national rifle range, where German forces shot Edith Cavell and resistance members in both world wars.

Brussels.name: Royal Museums of Fine Arts
places: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium
Brussels.description: Belgium’s main art museums, from Flemish old masters to the Magritte Museum, in connected buildings near Place Royale.

Bucharest.name: Revolution Square
Bucharest.description: The square where the 1989 revolution came to a head, lined by the former Communist Party headquarters and the old Royal Palace.

Bucharest.name: Palace of the Parliament
Bucharest.description: Ceaușescu’s enormous government palace, one of the largest buildings in the world, built over a cleared historic district. Guided tours run inside.

Bucharest.name: Romanian Athenaeum
Bucharest.description: A domed 19th-century concert hall, home of the city’s philharmonic orchestra, with a painted fresco running around the main hall.

Bucharest.name: University Square
Bucharest.description: A busy central square by the university, scene of street fighting in the 1989 revolution and of a long anti-government protest in 1990.

Budapest.name: Hungarian Parliament
places: Gyula Andrássy equestrian statue, Kossuth Square
Budapest.description: The huge Gothic Revival parliament on the Danube and the square in front. Guided tours take you inside to see the Holy Crown.

Budapest.name: Heroes’ Square
Budapest.description: A wide square at the end of Andrássy Avenue, with a column and statues of Hungary’s founding chieftains and kings, between two art museums.

Budapest.name: House of Terror
Budapest.description: A museum in the former headquarters of the fascist and then communist secret police, about the people they imprisoned, tortured and killed.

Budapest.name: Széchenyi Chain Bridge
Budapest.description: The first permanent bridge across the Danube in Budapest, opened in 1849, joining Pest to Buda below Castle Hill.

Budapest.name: Dohány Street Synagogue
places: Hungarian Jewish Museum (site of Herzl’s birthplace)
Budapest.description: Europe’s largest synagogue, with the Hungarian Jewish Museum next door and a Holocaust memorial garden behind.

Budapest.name: Great Market Hall
Budapest.description: Budapest’s largest covered market, from 1897, with produce and paprika stalls downstairs and food counters and souvenirs upstairs.

Budapest.name: Liberty Bridge
places: Kermit the Frog statue, Liberty Bridge
Budapest.description: A green steel bridge across the Danube, with mythical turul birds on top of its towers, leading to the Gellért Baths.

Budapest.name: Budapest Operetta Theatre
Budapest.description: A theatre on Nagymező Street devoted to operetta and musicals, the light-opera form Budapest is known for.

Budapest.name: Shoes on the Danube Bank
places: Shoes on the Danube Bank memorial
Budapest.description: Sixty pairs of iron shoes on the river bank, a memorial to the Jews shot into the Danube by Arrow Cross militiamen in 1944–45.

Budapest.name: Hungarian State Opera
Budapest.description: A neo-Renaissance opera house on Andrássy Avenue, opened in 1884, with a gilded auditorium. Guided tours run inside.

Budapest.name: Matthias Church
Budapest.description: A Gothic church on Castle Hill with a colourful tiled roof, where Hungary’s last kings were crowned. Fisherman’s Bastion is beside it.

Budapest.name: Liszt Academy of Music
Budapest.description: Hungary’s top music school and one of its main concert halls, in an Art Nouveau building on Liszt Ferenc Square.

Budapest.name: Bartók Memorial House
Budapest.description: The composer Béla Bartók’s last Budapest home, in the Buda hills, kept as a museum with his furniture, plus a small concert hall.

Budapest.name: Puskás Aréna
Budapest.description: Hungary’s national football stadium, opened in 2019, which also hosts big concerts.

Budapest.name: Columbo statue
Budapest.description: A life-size bronze statue of the TV detective Columbo and his dog, on Falk Miksa Street.

Copenhagen.name: Copenhagen City Hall
Copenhagen.description: The red-brick city hall and the big square in front, next to Tivoli. Inside is an astronomical clock, and the tower can be climbed.

Copenhagen.name: Højbro Plads
Copenhagen.description: An old-town square with a statue of Bishop Absalon on horseback, facing across the canal to Christiansborg Palace.

Copenhagen.name: Kongens Nytorv
Copenhagen.description: Copenhagen’s largest square, at the head of Nyhavn, with an equestrian statue of King Christian V in the middle.

Copenhagen.name: Royal Danish Theatre
places: Royal Danish Theatre (Old Stage), Kongens Nytorv
Copenhagen.description: The national theatre’s 1874 building on Kongens Nytorv, the home stage of the Royal Danish Ballet.

Copenhagen.name: Little Mermaid
Copenhagen.description: A small bronze statue of the fairy-tale mermaid, sitting on a rock by the harbour at Langelinie since 1913.

Copenhagen.name: Radisson Collection Royal Hotel
Copenhagen.description: A 1960 modernist hotel tower opposite Tivoli, with furniture and fittings designed by the same architect as the building.

Copenhagen.name: Assistens Cemetery
Copenhagen.description: A leafy cemetery in Nørrebro that locals use as a park, and the resting place of many well-known Danes, Kierkegaard among them.

Copenhagen.name: Danish Jewish Museum
Copenhagen.description: A museum of Danish Jewish history, including the 1943 rescue to Sweden, with an angular interior built inside an old royal boathouse.

Copenhagen.name: Nyhavn
Copenhagen.description: A 17th-century canal lined with colourful old townhouses, wooden ships and outdoor cafés, running from Kongens Nytorv to the harbour.

Copenhagen.name: CopenHill
Copenhagen.description: A waste-to-energy power plant with an artificial ski slope, a hiking trail and a climbing wall on its roof and walls.

Dublin.name: National Museum of Ireland – Archaeology
Dublin.description: Ireland’s archaeology museum on Kildare Street, with prehistoric gold, Viking finds and bog bodies.

Dublin.name: Trinity College
places: Book of Kells, Old Library, Trinity College
Dublin.description: Ireland’s oldest university, founded in 1592. Its Old Library holds the Book of Kells, a medieval illuminated gospel book.

Dublin.name: The Spire
Dublin.description: A 120-metre stainless-steel needle in the middle of O’Connell Street, put up in 2003 where Nelson’s Pillar once stood.

Dublin.name: General Post Office
Dublin.description: Dublin’s main post office, headquarters of the rebels in the 1916 Easter Rising. A museum inside tells the story.

Dublin.name: 14 Henrietta Street
Dublin.description: A Georgian townhouse museum showing its life as a grand home and later as a crowded tenement, through to the 1970s.

Dublin.name: The Cobblestone
Dublin.description: A pub in Smithfield known for its nightly traditional Irish music sessions.

Dublin.name: St Stephen’s Green
Dublin.description: A Victorian park in a Georgian square at the top of Grafton Street, with a lake, bridges and statues.

Dublin.name: Dublin Castle
Dublin.description: The former seat of British rule in Ireland, with state apartments, courtyards, and the Chester Beatty museum of manuscripts in its grounds.

Edinburgh.name: Palace of Holyroodhouse
Edinburgh.description: The monarch’s official residence in Scotland, at the foot of the Royal Mile, with Mary Queen of Scots’ rooms and a ruined abbey.

Edinburgh.name: Edinburgh Castle
Edinburgh.description: The fortress on a volcanic rock above the city, with the Scottish crown jewels, and the esplanade in front where the Tattoo is held.

Edinburgh.name: National Museum of Scotland
Edinburgh.description: A big museum of Scottish history, science and world cultures, with a rooftop terrace and Dolly the sheep.

Edinburgh.name: Writers’ Museum
Edinburgh.description: A 17th-century house off the Royal Mile with displays on Robert Burns, Walter Scott and Robert Louis Stevenson.

Edinburgh.name: St Giles’ Cathedral
places: Heart of Midlothian mosaic (site of the Old Tolbooth)
Edinburgh.description: Edinburgh’s main church, on the Royal Mile. In the cobbles outside, a heart marks the site of the old town prison.

Edinburgh.name: Greyfriars Kirkyard
Edinburgh.description: An old churchyard full of carved tombstones, with the statue of Greyfriars Bobby, the loyal terrier, by its gate.

Edinburgh.name: Princes Street Gardens
Edinburgh.description: A park in the valley below the castle, home to the Gothic spire of the Scott Monument, which you can climb.

Edinburgh.name: Surgeons’ Hall Museums
Edinburgh.description: Medical museums run by the Royal College of Surgeons, with anatomy and pathology collections and the history of surgery in the city.

Edinburgh.name: Scottish Parliament
Edinburgh.description: Scotland’s parliament building, opened in 2004, opposite Holyroodhouse. Visitors can tour it and watch debates.

Edinburgh.name: Scottish National Gallery
Edinburgh.description: Scotland’s national collection of fine art, from the Renaissance to the early 20th century, on the Mound above Princes Street Gardens.

Edinburgh.name: Old College
places: Site of Kirk o’ Field, Old College
Edinburgh.description: The university’s neoclassical quadrangle, built on the site of Kirk o’ Field, where Mary Queen of Scots’ husband was killed in 1567.

Florence.name: Uffizi Gallery
Florence.description: The great collection of Italian Renaissance painting, in the Medici’s former offices by the Arno: Botticelli, Leonardo, Michelangelo and more.

Florence.name: Museo Galileo
Florence.description: A science museum with the Medici’s scientific instruments, globes and maps, and Galileo’s own telescopes.

Florence.name: Florence Cathedral
places: Duomo central doorway, facing the Baptistery
Florence.description: The cathedral with Brunelleschi’s dome, its bell tower and the octagonal Baptistery, around the square at the heart of the city.

Florence.name: Museo dell’Opera del Duomo
Florence.description: The cathedral museum, holding the original Baptistery doors, sculpture from the cathedral and Michelangelo’s late Pietà.

Florence.name: Piazza della Signoria
places: Loggia dei Lanzi, Piazza della Signoria
Florence.description: Florence’s main civic square, with the Neptune fountain, a copy of Michelangelo’s David, and statues in the open-air Loggia dei Lanzi.

Florence.name: Palazzo Vecchio
places: Hall of the Five Hundred, Palazzo Vecchio
Florence.description: The fortress-like town hall on Piazza della Signoria, with painted state rooms including the vast Hall of the Five Hundred.

Florence.name: Piazza della Repubblica
Florence.description: A big 19th-century square on the site of the Roman forum, with a carousel, a triumphal arch and old cafés.

Florence.name: Palazzo Medici Riccardi
Florence.description: The Medici family’s 15th-century palace, with a small chapel covered in frescoes of the procession of the Magi.

Florence.name: Orsanmichele
Florence.description: A former grain market turned church, with statues of patron saints in niches on its outside walls, made for the city’s guilds.

Florence.name: San Lorenzo
Florence.description: The Medici family’s parish church, designed by Brunelleschi, with a bare unfinished facade and the Old Sacristy inside.

Florence.name: Laurentian Library
Florence.description: The Medici library in the cloister of San Lorenzo, designed by Michelangelo, with a sculptural staircase and a long reading room.

Florence.name: Medici Chapels
Florence.description: The Medici family tombs behind San Lorenzo, including Michelangelo’s New Sacristy, with a room below where he may have hidden in 1530.

Florence.name: Santa Croce
Florence.description: A large Franciscan church with the tombs of Michelangelo, Galileo and Machiavelli, the Pazzi Chapel, and a square in front.

Florence.name: Bargello Museum
Florence.description: A medieval palace and former prison, now Florence’s museum of Renaissance sculpture, with works by Donatello and Michelangelo.

Florence.name: Ponte Vecchio
Florence.description: A medieval bridge over the Arno lined with jewellers’ shops, with the Vasari Corridor, a private Medici passage, running along the top.

Florence.name: Piazzale Michelangelo
Florence.description: A hilltop square across the Arno with a wide view over the city and a bronze copy of David.

Florence.name: Accademia Gallery
Florence.description: The museum that holds Michelangelo’s David, along with his unfinished Prisoners and Florentine paintings.

Florence.name: Palazzo Pitti
Florence.description: A huge palace across the Arno that became the Medici’s home, now a group of museums, with the Boboli Gardens behind.

Florence.name: Santa Maria Novella
Florence.description: A Dominican church near the station with a striped marble facade, frescoes and Masaccio’s Trinity, facing its own square.

Florence.name: Brancacci Chapel
places: Brancacci Chapel, Santa Maria del Carmine
Florence.description: A chapel in the church of Santa Maria del Carmine, covered in early Renaissance frescoes by Masaccio and Masolino.

Florence.name: Santo Spirito
Florence.description: A Brunelleschi church in the Oltrarno with a plain facade, a wooden crucifix attributed to Michelangelo, and a lively square in front.

Helsinki.name: Senate Square
Helsinki.description: The city’s main neoclassical square, with the white, green-domed Helsinki Cathedral at the top of its wide steps.

Helsinki.name: Olympic Stadium
Helsinki.description: A white functionalist stadium built for the 1940 Olympics, which were cancelled; the Games came in 1952. Its tall tower has views over the city.

Helsinki.name: Oodi Central Library
Helsinki.description: A free public library opened in 2018 opposite Parliament, with a curved timber front, workshops with 3D printers and a big reading floor upstairs.

Helsinki.name: Finlandia Hall
Helsinki.description: A white marble concert and congress hall designed by Alvar Aalto, completed in 1971, on the shore of Töölö Bay.

Helsinki.name: Sibelius Monument
Helsinki.description: An abstract sculpture of hundreds of welded steel pipes, made in honour of the composer Jean Sibelius, in a small park by the sea.

Helsinki.name: Suomenlinna
Helsinki.description: An 18th-century sea fortress spread over a group of islands, a short ferry ride from the centre, with walls, tunnels, museums and cafés.

Helsinki.name: Hakaniemi Market
Helsinki.description: An open-air market square and its red-brick market hall from 1914, with stalls selling fish, meat, bread and Finnish food.

Istanbul.name: Hagia Sophia
Istanbul.description: Built as a cathedral in 537, it became a mosque in 1453, a museum in 1934 and a mosque again in 2020. Its huge dome still dominates the old city.

Istanbul.name: Topkapı Palace
Istanbul.description: The Ottoman sultans’ palace for nearly 400 years: a series of courtyards, the harem, the treasury and views over the Bosphorus.

Istanbul.name: Hippodrome
Istanbul.description: The long square on the site of the ancient chariot-racing track, with an Egyptian obelisk and other monuments along its middle.

Istanbul.name: Süleymaniye Mosque
Istanbul.description: The great 16th-century mosque on a hill above the Golden Horn, with a vast domed prayer hall, gardens and a cemetery.

Istanbul.name: Çemberlitaş Hamam
Istanbul.description: A Turkish bath built in 1584 and still in use, with separate domed marble halls for men and women.

Istanbul.name: Galata Bridge
Istanbul.description: The bridge across the Golden Horn, with a tram and road on top, fishermen along the rails, and fish restaurants on the lower level.

Istanbul.name: Rumeli Fortress
Istanbul.description: A fortress built by the Ottomans in 1452 on the European shore of the Bosphorus, a year before they took Constantinople.

Istanbul.name: Galata Tower
Istanbul.description: A round stone tower built by the Genoese in 1348, with a viewing balcony over the Golden Horn and the old city.

Istanbul.name: Galata Mevlevi Lodge
Istanbul.description: A former lodge of the Mevlevi order, the whirling dervishes, now a museum with the wooden hall where their ceremony took place.

Istanbul.name: Theodosian Walls
Istanbul.description: A stretch of the 5th-century walls that guarded Constantinople’s land side, at the gate named after the Ottoman cannon of the 1453 siege.

Istanbul.name: Grand Bazaar
Istanbul.description: One of the oldest and largest covered markets in the world: thousands of shops in a maze of vaulted lanes.

Kraków.name: Main Market Square
places: Adam Mickiewicz Monument, Main Market Square
Kraków.description: The huge medieval square at the heart of the old town, with the Cloth Hall in the middle and a museum of the city’s past underneath.

Kraków.name: St Mary’s Basilica
Kraków.description: The brick Gothic church on the Main Market Square, with a carved wooden altarpiece and a trumpet call played from its tower every hour.

Kraków.name: Central Square, Nowa Huta
Kraków.description: The main square of Nowa Huta, the socialist-realist steel town built in the 1950s on the city’s eastern edge.

Kraków.name: Oskar Schindler’s Enamel Factory
Kraków.description: Oskar Schindler’s former factory, now a museum about life in Kraków under Nazi occupation from 1939 to 1945.

Kraków.name: Piwnica pod Baranami
Kraków.description: A cellar cabaret under a palace on the Main Market Square, running since 1956, with cabaret and jazz evenings.

Kraków.name: Czartoryski Museum
Kraków.description: A museum of art and historical objects collected by the Czartoryski family, including Leonardo da Vinci’s Lady with an Ermine.

Kraków.name: Płaszów camp memorial
Kraków.description: The site of the Nazi labour and concentration camp at Płaszów, now an open hillside with memorials to those who were held and killed there.

Kraków.name: Wieliczka Salt Mine
Kraków.description: A salt mine worked for about 700 years just outside Kraków, with chambers, chapels and statues carved from rock salt deep underground.

Kraków.name: Wawel Cathedral
Kraków.description: The royal cathedral on Wawel Hill, where Polish kings were crowned and buried. The great Sigismund Bell hangs in its tower.

Lisbon.name: Largo do Carmo
Lisbon.description: A small square in Chiado beside the roofless ruins of the Carmo Convent, wrecked in the 1755 earthquake. The 1974 revolution ended here.

Lisbon.name: Praça do Comércio
Lisbon.description: The big riverside square rebuilt after the 1755 earthquake, with yellow arcades on three sides and a triumphal arch leading into the Baixa.

Lisbon.name: Praça dos Restauradores
Lisbon.description: A square with an obelisk marking Portugal’s 1640 break from Spanish rule, at the foot of the Avenida da Liberdade.

Lisbon.name: São Jorge Castle
places: São Jorge Castle (Castelo de São Jorge)
Lisbon.description: The hilltop castle above Alfama, with walls and towers to walk and views over the city and the river.

Lisbon.name: Rossio
Lisbon.description: The old town’s main square, with wave-patterned paving, two fountains and the national theatre on its north side.

Lisbon.name: São Domingos Church
places: Largo de São Domingos (1506 massacre memorial)
Lisbon.description: A church left scarred by a 1959 fire, and the small square beside it with a memorial to the Jews killed in the 1506 massacre.

Lisbon.name: Praça Luís de Camões
Lisbon.description: A square between Chiado and Bairro Alto, with a statue of the poet Luís de Camões in the middle.

Lisbon.name: Fado Museum
Lisbon.description: A museum of fado, Lisbon’s song of longing, at the edge of Alfama, with guitars, recordings and portraits of singers.

Lisbon.name: A Brasileira
Lisbon.description: A café in Chiado open since 1905, with a dark wood interior and a bronze statue of the poet Fernando Pessoa at a table outside.

Lisbon.name: National Pantheon
Lisbon.description: A domed baroque church that took nearly 300 years to finish, now the resting place of national figures, including the fado singer Amália Rodrigues.

Lisbon.name: Santa Luzia viewpoint
Lisbon.description: A terrace beside a small church in Alfama, with tiled panels on the walls and a view over the rooftops to the river.

Lisbon.name: 25 de Abril Bridge
Lisbon.description: The red suspension bridge over the Tagus, opened in 1966 and renamed after the 1974 revolution.

Lisbon.name: Mercado da Ribeira
Lisbon.description: The city’s old riverside market hall, with fresh produce stalls on one side and a big food hall of restaurant counters on the other.

Lisbon.name: Jerónimos Monastery
Lisbon.description: A huge 16th-century monastery in Belém, carved in the ornate Manueline style, with the tomb of Vasco da Gama.

Lisbon.name: Monument to the Discoveries
Lisbon.description: A 52-metre monument on the Belém riverfront, shaped like a ship’s prow, lined with figures from Portugal’s age of exploration.

Lisbon.name: Maritime Museum
Lisbon.description: A museum of Portuguese seafaring in a wing of the Jerónimos Monastery, with model ships, maps, instruments and royal barges.

Lisbon.name: Gulbenkian Museum
Lisbon.description: An art museum in a modernist building and garden, with one man’s collection running from ancient Egypt to art nouveau jewellery.

London.name: National Gallery
London.description: The national collection of European painting from the 1200s to 1900, on the north side of Trafalgar Square. Entry is free.

London.name: Trafalgar Square
London.description: The big public square with Nelson’s Column, fountains and bronze lions, and the old official measures of length set into its steps.

London.name: British Museum
London.description: A huge free museum of world history and culture in Bloomsbury, with the Rosetta Stone, Egyptian mummies and the Parthenon sculptures.

London.name: Tate Britain
London.description: The national gallery of British art from 1500 to today, on the river at Millbank, with a large collection of Turner. Entry is free.

London.name: Courtauld Gallery
London.description: A small gallery in Somerset House with a fine collection of Impressionist and Post-Impressionist paintings, plus Old Masters.

London.name: Monument to the Great Fire
places: Monument to the Great Fire of London
London.description: A stone column near where the Great Fire of 1666 began. You can climb its 311 steps to a viewing platform.

London.name: Palace of Westminster
London.description: The riverside home of the Houses of Parliament, rebuilt in Gothic style after a fire in 1834, with the clock tower that holds Big Ben.

London.name: Parliament Square
London.description: A green square between Parliament and Westminster Abbey, ringed with statues of statesmen and a frequent site of protests.

London.name: St Paul’s Cathedral
London.description: The domed cathedral rebuilt after the Great Fire of 1666, with galleries up in the dome and crypts below.

London.name: Tate Modern
London.description: The national gallery of modern and contemporary art, in a former power station on the South Bank. Entry to the collection is free.

London.name: Tower of London
places: Yeoman Warders’ Club, Tower of London
London.description: The medieval fortress on the Thames, once a royal palace and prison, now home to the Crown Jewels and the Yeoman Warders.

London.name: Covent Garden Market
London.description: The old fruit and vegetable market hall in the West End, now shops, stalls and cafés, with street performers in the piazza.

London.name: John Snow pump
London.description: A replica water pump in Soho marking where, in 1854, a doctor traced a cholera outbreak to a contaminated well.

London.name: 430 King’s Road
London.description: The Chelsea shop where Malcolm McLaren and Vivienne Westwood sold clothes in the 1970s, at the centre of the early punk scene.

London.name: Gay’s the Word
London.description: Britain’s oldest LGBT bookshop, open in Bloomsbury since 1979.

London.name: Shakespeare’s Globe
London.description: A reconstruction of Shakespeare’s open-air playhouse on the South Bank, opened in 1997, where plays are staged much as they were around 1600.

London.name: Roman wall at Tower Hill
London.description: One of the best-surviving stretches of the Roman wall that once enclosed London, beside Tower Hill station.

London.name: Royal Albert Hall
London.description: The round, domed concert hall in South Kensington, opened in 1871, home every summer to the Proms.

London.name: Buckingham Palace
London.description: The monarch’s London home and office, at the end of the Mall. The state rooms open to visitors in summer.

London.name: British Library
London.description: The national library of the UK, in a red-brick building next to St Pancras, with a free gallery of manuscripts such as Magna Carta.

London.name: Beigel Bake
London.description: A bagel bakery on Brick Lane, open 24 hours, known for its salt beef bagels.

London.name: Victoria and Albert Museum
places: Cast Courts, Victoria and Albert Museum
London.description: A huge free museum of art and design in South Kensington, including the Cast Courts, halls of plaster copies of famous sculpture and buildings.

London.name: Thames Barrier
London.description: A row of steel flood gates across the Thames at Woolwich, in use since 1982 to protect London from tidal surges.

London.name: Dulwich Picture Gallery
London.description: England’s oldest public art gallery, opened in 1817 in south London, with a collection of Old Master paintings.

London.name: Westminster Abbey
places: Henry VII Lady Chapel, Westminster Abbey
London.description: The Gothic abbey church where English and British monarchs are crowned, and many are buried, including in the fan-vaulted Lady Chapel.

London.name: London Mithraeum
places: London Mithraeum (Temple of Mithras), Bloomberg building
London.description: The remains of a Roman temple to the god Mithras, shown in the basement of the Bloomberg building in the City. Entry is free.

Madrid.name: Prado Museum
places: Goya Monument, beside the Prado Museum
Madrid.description: Spain’s national art museum, built on the royal collections: Velázquez, Goya, El Greco and Bosch. A statue of Goya stands outside.

Madrid.name: Puerta del Sol
Madrid.description: Madrid’s busiest square. A plaque on the pavement marks kilometre zero of Spain’s roads, and crowds gather under the clock on New Year’s Eve.

Madrid.name: Plaza Mayor
Madrid.description: A big arcaded 17th-century square in the old town, once used for markets, bullfights and public executions.

Madrid.name: Las Ventas bullring
Madrid.description: Madrid’s bullring, a large brick and tile building from the 1930s in neo-Mudéjar style. It also hosts concerts.

Madrid.name: Congress of Deputies
Madrid.description: The lower house of Spain’s parliament, in a 19th-century building guarded by two bronze lions.

Madrid.name: Santiago Bernabéu Stadium
Madrid.description: Real Madrid’s home stadium on the Paseo de la Castellana, with a club museum and stadium tour.

Madrid.name: Atocha station
Madrid.description: Madrid’s main railway station, built around a 19th-century iron and glass train hall.

Madrid.name: Valley of the Fallen
Madrid.description: A basilica cut into a mountain outside Madrid under a huge stone cross, built by Franco’s regime partly with prisoners’ labour.

Madrid.name: Reina Sofía Museum
Madrid.description: Spain’s national museum of modern and contemporary art, in a former hospital. Picasso’s Guernica hangs here.

Madrid.name: Royal Palace of Aranjuez
Madrid.description: A royal palace with large gardens in the town of Aranjuez, south of Madrid, long used by Spanish kings as a spring residence.

Madrid.name: Plaza de Santa Ana
places: Lorca statue, Plaza de Santa Ana
Madrid.description: A lively square in the old literary quarter, lined with bars and the Teatro Español, with a statue of the poet Lorca.

Madrid.name: El Escorial
places: Friars’ Garden, Royal Monastery of El Escorial
Madrid.description: A vast 16th-century monastery and royal palace in the hills northwest of Madrid, with a basilica, library, royal tombs and terraced gardens.

Manchester.name: The Haçienda (site)
places: Site of the Haçienda club, Whitworth Street West
Manchester.description: The site of the Haçienda nightclub (1982–97), the centre of the city’s acid house scene. The building that replaced it is flats named after it.

Manchester.name: Free Trade Hall
Manchester.description: A Victorian hall on the site of the Peterloo Massacre, for a century the city’s main concert hall. It is now a hotel.

Manchester.name: Old Trafford
Manchester.description: Manchester United’s home stadium, just outside the city centre, with a club museum and stadium tours.

Manchester.name: Manchester Central Library
Manchester.description: The city’s main public library, a round domed building from the 1930s on St Peter’s Square, with a large reading room under the dome.

Manchester.name: Chetham’s Library
Manchester.description: A public library founded in 1653 in a medieval building near the cathedral, often called the oldest in the English-speaking world.

Manchester.name: Pankhurst Centre
Manchester.description: The house where Emmeline Pankhurst founded the Women’s Social and Political Union in 1903, now a small museum and women’s centre.

Manchester.name: Salford Lads Club
Manchester.description: A youth club opened in 1903 that is still running. Fans of The Smiths come to photograph the doorway seen in the band’s 1986 album artwork.

Manchester.name: St Peter’s Square
Manchester.description: A city-centre square on part of the site of the 1819 Peterloo Massacre, when cavalry charged a peaceful crowd calling for the vote.

Manchester.name: Manchester Town Hall
Manchester.description: The Victorian Gothic town hall on Albert Square, finished in 1877, with murals of the city’s history in the Great Hall.

Marseille.name: Old Port
Marseille.description: The old harbour at the heart of the city, lined with cafés and moored boats, with a small fish market on the quay most mornings.

Marseille.name: Château d’If
Marseille.description: A 16th-century fortress and former prison on an island in the bay, the setting of The Count of Monte Cristo. Boats leave from the Old Port.

Marseille.name: Cité Radieuse
Marseille.description: Le Corbusier’s 1952 concrete housing block on stilts, with shops and a hotel on an inside street and a terrace on the roof.

Munich.name: Marienplatz
Munich.description: Munich’s main square, in front of the neo-Gothic New Town Hall, whose tower has a mechanical Glockenspiel that plays most days at 11am.

Munich.name: Ludwig Maximilian University
Munich.description: The university’s main building, where White Rose students were arrested in 1943 for spreading anti-Nazi leaflets. A memorial is inside.

Munich.name: Alte Pinakothek
Munich.description: One of the oldest public galleries in the world, opened in 1836, with European paintings from the Middle Ages to the 18th century.

Munich.name: Residenz
Munich.description: The city palace of Bavaria’s rulers: courtyards, state rooms, a treasury and a small rococo court theatre.

Munich.name: Olympic Stadium
Munich.description: The stadium built for the 1972 Olympics, under a tent-like roof of acrylic panels, in a park laid out on wartime rubble.

Munich.name: Connollystraße 31
Munich.description: The building in the Olympic Village where Israeli athletes were taken hostage during the 1972 Olympics. A plaque marks it.

Munich.name: Nymphenburg Palace
Munich.description: The baroque summer palace of Bavaria’s rulers, with large gardens and the Gallery of Beauties, a room of portraits of women.

Munich.name: Odeonsplatz
Munich.description: A grand square at the south end of Ludwigstraße, with the Feldherrnhalle loggia and the yellow Theatine Church.

Munich.name: Hofbräuhaus
Munich.description: A huge beer hall that began as the royal brewery in 1589, with long shared tables, a brass band and its own beer.

Munich.name: Isartor
Munich.description: One of three surviving gates of the medieval city wall, on the east side of the old town.

Munich.name: Glyptothek
Munich.description: A museum of ancient Greek and Roman sculpture in a temple-like building on Königsplatz, opened in 1830.

Munich.name: Führerbau
places: Führerbau, now the University of Music and Performing Arts
Munich.description: A Nazi party building on Königsplatz where the 1938 Munich Agreement was signed. It is now a university of music.

Munich.name: National Theatre (Bavarian State Opera)
Munich.description: The neoclassical opera house on Max-Joseph-Platz, home of the Bavarian State Opera and Ballet, rebuilt after wartime bombing.

Munich.name: Bavarian State Library
Munich.description: One of Europe’s largest research libraries, in a long 19th-century building on Ludwigstraße.

Munich.name: Musicland Studios
Munich.description: A former recording studio in the basement of the Arabella high-rise, where many rock and disco records were made in the 1970s and 80s.

Munich.name: Kurt Eisner memorial
Munich.description: A memorial set into the pavement where Kurt Eisner, Bavaria’s first republican prime minister, was shot dead in 1919.

Munich.name: Hofgarten arcades
places: Hofgarten arcades, site of the 1937 Degenerate Art show
Munich.description: The arcades around the old court garden beside the Residenz, where the Nazis’ 1937 ‘Degenerate Art’ exhibition was held.

Munich.name: Allianz Arena
Munich.description: FC Bayern’s stadium on the northern edge of the city, wrapped in panels that light up at night, with the club museum inside.

Naples.name: National Archaeological Museum
Naples.description: One of the great collections of ancient Roman art, with mosaics, frescoes and objects found at Pompeii and Herculaneum.

Naples.name: Stadio Diego Armando Maradona
Naples.description: SSC Napoli’s home stadium in the Fuorigrotta district, renamed after Diego Maradona in 2020.

Naples.name: Vele di Scampia
Naples.description: Huge sail-shaped public housing blocks from the 1960s and 70s in the northern suburb of Scampia, partly demolished since the 1990s.

Naples.name: Pompeii
Naples.description: The Roman town buried by Vesuvius in AD 79, south of Naples. Porta Marina is the main gate into its excavated streets and houses.

Naples.name: Piazza del Mercato
Naples.description: A large square near the port that was for centuries the city’s main market and its place of public executions.

Naples.name: Pio Monte della Misericordia
Naples.description: A small 17th-century church run by a charity, with Caravaggio’s Seven Works of Mercy above the altar.

Naples.name: Pizzeria Brandi
Naples.description: An old pizzeria near Piazza del Plebiscito that claims the margherita pizza was first made here, in 1889.

Naples.name: Mount Vesuvius
Naples.description: The volcano that buried Pompeii in AD 79 and last erupted in 1944. A path leads up to the rim of the crater.

Naples.name: Castel Nuovo
Naples.description: A medieval castle by the port with five round towers and a white marble triumphal arch at the entrance. It houses the civic museum.

Oslo.name: MUNCH
Oslo.description: A tall museum on the harbour front devoted to Edvard Munch, with thousands of his paintings, prints and drawings.

Oslo.name: Fram Museum
Oslo.description: A museum on the Bygdøy peninsula built around the polar ship Fram, which you can go aboard, and the history of polar exploration.

Oslo.name: Kon-Tiki Museum
Oslo.description: A museum on Bygdøy holding the balsa raft Kon-Tiki, sailed across the Pacific in 1947, and other boats from Thor Heyerdahl’s voyages.

Oslo.name: Oslo City Hall
Oslo.description: The brick city hall with two towers on the harbour, where the Nobel Peace Prize is presented each December. The halls are covered in murals.

Oslo.name: Royal Palace
Oslo.description: The king’s official residence, at the top of Karl Johans gate, in a public park, with a daily changing of the guard.

Oslo.name: Helvete record shop (former)
places: Former Helvete record shop, Schweigaards gate
Oslo.description: A former record shop near the central station that was the meeting place of Norway’s early-1990s black metal scene.

Oslo.name: Museum of the Viking Age
places: Museum of the Viking Age (Viking Ship Museum)
Oslo.description: The museum on Bygdøy built for three Viking ships found in burial mounds, being rebuilt and enlarged as the Museum of the Viking Age.

Oslo.name: National Museum
Oslo.description: Norway’s largest art museum, opened in 2022 by the harbour, with art and design from ancient times to today, including Munch’s The Scream.

Oslo.name: Akershus Fortress
Oslo.description: A medieval castle and fortress on the harbour, later a royal residence, with ramparts you can walk and a museum of the wartime resistance.

Paris.name: Louvre
places: Salle des États (Mona Lisa room), Louvre Museum
Paris.description: The former royal palace turned art museum, entered through a glass pyramid. Its collection runs from ancient Egypt to the Mona Lisa.

Paris.name: Musée d’Orsay
Paris.description: A museum in a former railway station on the Left Bank, with the largest collection of Impressionist and Post-Impressionist painting.

Paris.name: Palais Garnier
Paris.description: The 19th-century opera house, with a grand marble staircase and a ceiling painted by Chagall. It hosts opera and ballet.

Paris.name: Notre-Dame Cathedral
Paris.description: The Gothic cathedral on the Île de la Cité, reopened in 2024 after the 2019 fire. A plaque in the square marks the point distances in France are measured from.

Paris.name: Eiffel Tower
Paris.description: The wrought-iron tower built for the 1889 World’s Fair, with lifts and stairs up to viewing platforms over the city.

Paris.name: Palace of Versailles
Paris.description: The vast palace and gardens of Louis XIV, outside Paris, with the Hall of Mirrors and the royal apartments.

Paris.name: Musée de l’Orangerie
Paris.description: A small museum in the Tuileries Garden, built around two oval rooms that hold Monet’s Water Lilies panels.

Paris.name: Centre Pompidou
Paris.description: France’s national museum of modern art, in a 1977 building with its pipes, ducts and escalators on the outside.

Paris.name: Le Meurice
places: Le Meurice hotel, Rue de Rivoli
Paris.description: A luxury hotel on the Rue de Rivoli facing the Tuileries. During the Occupation it was the headquarters of the German military command in Paris.

Paris.name: Père Lachaise Cemetery
places: Édith Piaf’s grave, Père Lachaise Cemetery
Paris.description: The city’s largest cemetery, on a hill in the east, with Édith Piaf’s grave and the wall where the last Communards were shot in 1871.

Paris.name: Place de la Concorde
places: Luxor Obelisk, Place de la Concorde
Paris.description: The largest square in Paris, where the guillotine stood during the Revolution. At its centre is an Egyptian obelisk over 3,000 years old.

Paris.name: Place de la Bastille
Paris.description: The square where the Bastille prison stood until it was stormed in 1789. A column marks the centre, and traces of the fortress survive in the Métro station.

Paris.name: Place du Trocadéro
Paris.description: A square across the river from the Eiffel Tower, with terraces that give one of the classic views of it.

Paris.name: Shakespeare and Company
Paris.description: An English-language bookshop on the Left Bank, across the river from Notre-Dame, crammed with new and second-hand books.

Paris.name: Pont des Arts
Paris.description: A footbridge across the Seine between the Louvre and the Institut de France, once covered in love padlocks.

Paris.name: Pont Neuf
Paris.description: Despite its name (‘New Bridge’), the oldest standing bridge across the Seine in Paris, finished in 1607 across the tip of the Île de la Cité.

Paris.name: Carnavalet Museum
Paris.description: The free museum of the history of Paris, in two mansions in the Marais, with old shop signs, period rooms and relics of the Revolution.

Paris.name: Folies Bergère
Paris.description: A music hall open since 1869 and famous for its cabaret revues. It now mostly hosts concerts and musicals.

Paris.name: Les Invalides
Paris.description: Louis XIV’s military hospital under a gilded dome. It now holds Napoleon’s tomb, the army museum and a museum of scale models of fortified towns.

Paris.name: Hôtel de Ville
Paris.description: Paris’s city hall, a 19th-century rebuilding of a Renaissance original, and the square in front, where public executions once took place.

Prague.name: Prague Castle
Prague.description: A huge castle complex on the hill above the Vltava, seat of Czech rulers for over a thousand years, including the Old Royal Palace.

Prague.name: St Vitus Cathedral
Prague.description: The Gothic cathedral inside Prague Castle, where Czech kings were crowned and buried, with a stained-glass window by Alfons Mucha.

Prague.name: Old Town Hall and Astronomical Clock
Prague.description: The medieval astronomical clock on the Old Town Hall, first installed in 1410. On the hour, figures of the apostles appear in windows above the dials.

Prague.name: Old Town Square
Prague.description: The main square of the old town, ringed by pastel houses, the Old Town Hall and the twin towers of the Týn Church.

Prague.name: Wenceslas Square
Prague.description: A long, wide square in the New Town, scene of the mass protests of 1989. A statue of St Wenceslas stands at the top end.

Prague.name: Melantrich building
Prague.description: A building on Wenceslas Square from whose balcony dissident leaders addressed the crowds during the Velvet Revolution in 1989.

Prague.name: Municipal House
Prague.description: An Art Nouveau civic building from 1912, next to the Powder Tower, with the Smetana Hall concert hall, a café and a restaurant.

Prague.name: New City Hall
Prague.description: The early-1900s seat of Prague’s city government, on Mariánské Square, with large sculptures at its corners.

Prague.name: Church of Sts Cyril and Methodius
places: Church of Sts Cyril and Methodius, Resslova
Prague.description: An Orthodox church where the Czech parachutists who assassinated Reinhard Heydrich hid and died in 1942. Its crypt is now a memorial.

Prague.name: Old Jewish Cemetery
Prague.description: One of Europe’s oldest Jewish burial grounds, in the Jewish Quarter, with some 12,000 tombstones crowded together, many of them tilting.

Prague.name: Old-New Synagogue
Prague.description: Europe’s oldest active synagogue, a 13th-century Gothic building in the Jewish Quarter. Legend says the Golem lies in its attic.

Prague.name: Estates Theatre
Prague.description: An 18th-century theatre in the old town where Mozart’s Don Giovanni premiered in 1787. It still stages opera, drama and ballet.

Prague.name: Charles Bridge
Prague.description: The 14th-century stone bridge across the Vltava, lined with baroque statues of saints and busy from early morning to late at night.

Reykjavík.name: Austurvöllur
Reykjavík.description: A small grassy square in the centre, facing the Parliament building and the cathedral, with a statue of the independence leader Jón Sigurðsson.

Reykjavík.name: Harpa
Reykjavík.description: The glass-fronted concert hall on the harbour, opened in 2011 and home of the Iceland Symphony Orchestra.

Reykjavík.name: Lækjartorg
Reykjavík.description: A small square in the city centre, where Lækjargata meets Austurstræti, long used as a meeting point and for public gatherings.

Reykjavík.name: Hallgrímskirkja
Reykjavík.description: The concrete Lutheran church on the hill above the centre, with a 74.5 m tower you can go up. A statue of Leif Erikson stands in front.

Reykjavík.name: University of Iceland
Reykjavík.description: Iceland’s oldest and largest university, founded in 1911, on a campus just south of the city centre next to the National Museum.

Reykjavík.name: Kaffibarinn
Reykjavík.description: A small downtown bar in an old house just off Laugavegur, a fixture of the city’s nightlife since the 1990s and a setting in the film 101 Reykjavík.

Reykjavík.name: Höfði House
Reykjavík.description: A white wooden house by the shore, built in 1909, where the US and Soviet leaders Reagan and Gorbachev held their 1986 summit.

Reykjavík.name: Laugardalshöll
Reykjavík.description: The city’s main indoor sports and concert hall, where the 1972 world chess championship between Fischer and Spassky was played.

Reykjavík.name: Icelandic Phallological Museum
Reykjavík.description: A museum devoted to penises, with a large collection of specimens from Iceland’s land and sea mammals, in the Hafnartorg development by the harbour.

Rome.name: Capitoline Museums
places: Palazzo dei Conservatori courtyard, Capitoline Museums
Rome.description: Some of the world’s oldest public museums, in the palaces around Michelangelo’s square on the Capitoline Hill, with the bronze she-wolf.

Rome.name: St Peter’s Basilica
places: Chair of St Peter, St Peter’s Basilica
Rome.description: The Pope’s basilica and the colonnaded square in front. Inside are Michelangelo’s Pietà, Bernini’s bronze canopy and the Chair of St Peter.

Rome.name: Sistine Chapel
Rome.description: The papal chapel at the end of the Vatican Museums route, with Michelangelo’s ceiling and Last Judgement. Popes are elected here.

Rome.name: Vatican Museums
Rome.description: The popes’ art collections, spread through the Vatican palaces: ancient sculpture, Etruscan finds, the Raphael Rooms and a picture gallery.

Rome.name: Borghese Gallery
Rome.description: A 17th-century villa in the Borghese park holding sculptures by Bernini and paintings by Caravaggio. Entry is by timed booking only.

Rome.name: Colosseum
Rome.description: The amphitheatre finished in 80 AD, where gladiators fought in front of crowds of around 50,000.

Rome.name: Trevi Fountain
Rome.description: The largest baroque fountain in Rome, finished in 1762. Tradition says a coin thrown over your shoulder means you will come back.

Rome.name: Roman Forum
places: Temple of Antoninus and Faustina, Roman Forum
Arch of Septimius Severus, Roman Forum
Rome.description: The ruins of ancient Rome’s political and religious centre: temples, triumphal arches and the early frescoed church of Santa Maria Antiqua.

Rome.name: Castel Sant’Angelo
Rome.description: Hadrian’s mausoleum by the Tiber, later a papal fortress and prison. It is now a museum, with views from the terrace at the top.

Rome.name: Ponte Sant’Angelo
Rome.description: A Roman footbridge across the Tiber, built by Hadrian to reach his tomb, lined with ten baroque angels designed by Bernini.

Rome.name: Pantheon
Rome.description: A Roman temple from around 125 AD, now a church, with a huge unreinforced concrete dome open to the sky at the top.

Rome.name: Arch of Constantine
Rome.description: A triumphal arch beside the Colosseum, put up in 315 AD for the emperor Constantine, partly decorated with carvings taken from older monuments.

Rome.name: Largo di Torre Argentina
Rome.description: A sunken square of temple ruins next to the spot where Julius Caesar was killed. A cat shelter operates on the site.

Rome.name: Piazza Navona
places: Fountain of the Moor, Piazza Navona
Rome.description: A long baroque square on the outline of an ancient stadium, with three fountains, including Bernini’s Fountain of the Four Rivers.

Rome.name: Testaccio Market
Rome.description: A covered food market in the Testaccio neighbourhood, with produce stalls and counters selling Roman street food.

Rome.name: San Luigi dei Francesi
Rome.description: The church of the French community near Piazza Navona, with three Caravaggio paintings of the life of St Matthew in a side chapel.

Rome.name: Acqua Paola Fountain
Rome.description: A large early-1600s fountain on the Janiculum hill, built like a triumphal arch, with views across the city.

Rome.name: Santa Maria Maggiore
Rome.description: One of Rome’s four major papal basilicas, with fifth-century mosaics and a gilded coffered ceiling.

Rome.name: Baths of Caracalla
Rome.description: The huge brick ruins of a third-century public bath complex. Opera and concerts are staged here in summer.

Rome.name: Ara Pacis Museum
Rome.description: A glass-walled museum by the Tiber built around the Ara Pacis, a carved marble altar celebrating the peace brought by Augustus.

Rome.name: Circus Maximus
Rome.description: The site of ancient Rome’s chariot-racing stadium, now a long grassy hollow below the Palatine Hill.

Rome.name: Trajan’s Forum and Column
Rome.description: The last and largest of the imperial forums, with Trajan’s Column, carved with his wars in a spiral, and the brick market halls on the hillside.

Rome.name: San Pietro in Vincoli
Rome.description: A basilica that keeps the chains said to have bound St Peter, and Michelangelo’s statue of Moses on the tomb of Pope Julius II.

Rome.name: Santa Maria del Popolo
Rome.description: A church on Piazza del Popolo with two Caravaggio paintings, of St Paul and St Peter, and a chapel designed by Raphael.

Rome.name: National Etruscan Museum
Rome.description: A 16th-century papal villa, now the national museum of the Etruscans, the people who ruled central Italy before the Romans.

Rome.name: Palazzo Massimo
Rome.description: A branch of the National Roman Museum near Termini station, with ancient sculpture, bronzes and painted rooms from Roman villas.

Rome.name: Spanish Steps
Rome.description: A wide 18th-century stairway from Piazza di Spagna up to a church, with a boat-shaped fountain at the bottom.

Rome.name: Church of the Gesù
places: Chapel of St Ignatius, Church of the Gesù
Rome.description: The mother church of the Jesuits, with a painted ceiling that seems to open to the sky and the tomb of St Ignatius in a side chapel.

Rome.name: Sant’Andrea al Quirinale
places: Rooms of St Stanislas Kostka, Sant’Andrea al Quirinale
Rome.description: A small oval church by Bernini, with the rooms next door where the young Jesuit St Stanislas Kostka lived and died.

Seville.name: Seville Cathedral
places: Patio de los Naranjos, Seville Cathedral
Seville.description: A vast Gothic cathedral built on the site of a mosque. The mosque’s minaret became the Giralda bell tower, and its orange-tree courtyard survives.

Seville.name: Archive of the Indies
places: General Archive of the Indies (Archivo de Indias)
Seville.description: A 16th-century merchants’ exchange next to the cathedral, now holding the records of Spain’s empire in the Americas. Some rooms are open to visitors.

Seville.name: Real Alcázar
Seville.description: A royal palace begun in the Middle Ages, with Mudéjar halls, tiled courtyards and large gardens. The upper floors are still used by the Spanish royal family.

Seville.name: Plaza Nueva
Seville.description: A large open square by the city hall, with a statue of King Ferdinand III on horseback in the middle.

Seville.name: Alameda de Hércules
Seville.description: A long tree-lined promenade laid out in the 1500s, with old stone columns at each end, now lined with bars and busy at night.

Seville.name: Torre del Oro
Seville.description: A 13th-century Moorish watchtower on the riverbank, built to guard the port. Inside is a small naval museum, with views from the top.

Seville.name: Maestranza bullring
Seville.description: An 18th-century bullring by the river, one of the oldest in Spain, with a museum and guided tours.

Seville.name: Triana Bridge
Seville.description: A 19th-century iron bridge over the Guadalquivir, linking the centre with Triana, the old potters’ and flamenco quarter.

Seville.name: Royal Tobacco Factory
Seville.description: A huge 18th-century tobacco factory, now part of the university. Carmen, the heroine of Bizet’s opera, works here as a cigar-maker.

Seville.name: Hospital de la Caridad
Seville.description: A 17th-century almshouse near the river, still caring for the elderly, with a baroque church full of paintings by Murillo and Valdés Leal.

Stockholm.name: Vasa Museum
Stockholm.description: A museum built around the Vasa, a 17th-century warship that sank on its maiden voyage in 1628 and was raised almost intact in 1961.

Stockholm.name: Stortorget
Stockholm.description: The old town’s main square, ringed by tall merchants’ houses in red and ochre. In 1520 it was the scene of the Stockholm Bloodbath.

Stockholm.name: Sergels torg
Stockholm.description: The city’s central sunken plaza, with black-and-white triangle paving and a glass obelisk, next to the Kulturhuset arts centre.

Stockholm.name: Olof Palme murder site
Stockholm.description: The spot on Sveavägen where Prime Minister Olof Palme was shot dead in 1986, marked by a plaque in the pavement.

Stockholm.name: Norrmalmstorg
Stockholm.description: A city-centre square where a 1973 bank robbery and hostage siege gave the world the term “Stockholm syndrome”.

Stockholm.name: Drottningholm Palace
Stockholm.description: The Swedish royal family’s home, on an island west of the city, with baroque gardens and an 18th-century court theatre still in working order.

Stockholm.name: Kungsträdgården
Stockholm.description: A central park and public square, once the royal kitchen garden, used for outdoor events. Its cherry trees blossom in spring.

Stockholm.name: Parliament House
Stockholm.description: The home of Sweden’s parliament, the Riksdag, on a small island between the old town and the city centre.

Stockholm.name: Raoul Wallenbergs torg
Stockholm.description: A waterside square named after the Swedish diplomat who saved thousands of Hungarian Jews in 1944, with a memorial to him.

Stockholm.name: ABBA The Museum
Stockholm.description: A museum on Djurgården about the Swedish pop group, with stage costumes, gold records and rooms where you can sing along.

Venice.name: St Mark’s Basilica
places: Horses of St Mark, St Mark’s Basilica
Venice.description: Venice’s great square and the gold-mosaic basilica at its end, home of the bronze horses of St Mark and the Tetrarchs sculpture.

Venice.name: Doge’s Palace
places: Doge’s Palace and the Piombi prison cells
Hall of the Great Council, Doge’s Palace
Venice.description: The Gothic palace that ran the Venetian republic, with the vast Great Council hall, the Piombi prison cells and the Bridge of Sighs.

Venice.name: Rialto Bridge
Venice.description: The oldest bridge across the Grand Canal, a 16th-century stone arch lined with shops, next to the Rialto market.

Venice.name: La Fenice
Venice.description: Venice’s opera house, burned down and rebuilt more than once, most recently reopening in 2003. You can tour it by day.

Venice.name: Grand Hotel des Bains
places: Grand Hotel des Bains, Lido di Venezia
Venice.description: A Belle Époque beach hotel on the Lido, the setting of Thomas Mann’s Death in Venice. It has been closed since 2010.

Venice.name: Jewish Ghetto
places: Campo del Ghetto Nuovo, Jewish Ghetto
Jewish Ghetto, Campo del Ghetto Nuovo
Venice.description: The main square of the Ghetto, set up in 1516 and the origin of the word “ghetto”, with old synagogues and the Jewish Museum.

Venice.name: Corte del Milion
places: Corte del Milion, Marco Polo’s family home
Venice.description: A small courtyard near the Rialto where Marco Polo’s family lived. Their house later burned down, and a theatre now stands on the site.

Venice.name: Gallerie dell’Accademia
Venice.description: The city’s main collection of Venetian painting from the 1300s to the 1700s: Bellini, Giorgione, Titian, Tintoretto and Veronese.

Venice.name: Scuola Grande di San Rocco
Venice.description: A confraternity’s meeting house whose walls and ceilings are covered with more than 50 paintings by Tintoretto.

Venice.name: Frari church
places: Frari church (Santa Maria Gloriosa dei Frari)
Venice.description: A huge Gothic friars’ church with Titian’s Assumption over the high altar and the tombs of Titian and the composer Monteverdi.

Venice.name: San Barnaba
Venice.description: An 18th-century church and the canal-side square in front of it, in Dorsoduro. The church was a library in Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade.

Venice.name: La Pietà church
places: La Pietà church, Riva degli Schiavoni
Venice.description: The waterfront church of the orphanage where Vivaldi taught music, rebuilt after his death. It still hosts concerts.

Venice.name: Scuola Grande di San Marco
places: Ospedale Civile city hospital, Scuola Grande di San Marco
Venice.description: A Renaissance confraternity building with a marble trompe-l’œil façade, now the entrance to the city hospital and a museum of medical history.

Venice.name: Naval History Museum
places: Museo Storico Navale, naval history museum
Venice.description: A museum near the Arsenal on Venice’s life at sea, with ship models, weapons and a model of the doge’s ceremonial barge.

Venice.name: Arsenal gate
Venice.description: The Renaissance land gate of the Arsenal, the vast state shipyard that built Venice’s fleet, guarded by stone lions brought from Greece.

Venice.name: Torcello Cathedral
Venice.description: A cathedral founded in 639 on a now nearly empty island in the northern lagoon, with Byzantine mosaics including a huge Last Judgement.

Zurich.name: Paradeplatz
Zurich.description: A square on Bahnhofstrasse lined with the head offices of Swiss banks, plus the Sprüngli café and chocolate shop.

Zurich.name: Cabaret Voltaire
Zurich.description: The small old-town venue where the Dada art movement started in 1916, now an arts space and bar with exhibitions and events.

Zurich.name: Kunsthaus Zürich
Zurich.description: Zurich’s main art museum, with Swiss and European painting and sculpture and a large collection of work by Alberto Giacometti.

Zurich.name: Grossmünster
Zurich.description: A twin-towered Romanesque church by the river, where Zwingli launched the Swiss Reformation in the 1520s. You can climb one of the towers.

Zurich.name: Bürkliplatz
Zurich.description: A square on the lake at the end of Bahnhofstrasse, where the lake boats leave and a flea market runs on Saturdays in summer.

Zurich.name: Sechseläutenplatz
Zurich.description: A big open square between the opera house and the lake, where a snowman effigy is burned at the Sechseläuten spring festival.

Zurich.name: Rote Fabrik
Zurich.description: A former silk mill on the lakeshore, turned into an alternative arts centre after 1980s protests, with concerts, theatre and a restaurant.
